claim: The Museo de Cáceres spans 12 buildings in a 16th-century mansion built over a 12th-century aljibe (cistern) and its fine-arts display shows works by Picasso, Miró, Tàpies and El Greco.
quote: The excellent Museo de Cáceres, spread across 12 buildings in a 16th-century mansion built over an evocative 12th-century aljibe (cistern)... the equally appealing fine-arts display showcases works by such greats as Picasso, Miró, Tàpies and El Greco.

claim: The aljibe beneath the Palacio de las Veletas is the best-preserved Hispano-Muslim cistern in Spain, dating to the 11th-12th century with five naves separated by horseshoe arches.
quote: the best-preserved Hispano-Muslim aljibe, or cistern, in Spain, and one of the best in the world... formed by five naves separated by barrel vaults and horseshoe arches.

claim: The Museo de Cáceres is partially closed for renovation, with ethnography, fine-arts rooms and temporary exhibitions (Casa de los Caballos) shut until around 2026, leaving only the archaeology rooms and the cistern open.
quote: temporarily partially closed, initially until 2026, with the closure affecting the ethnography and fine arts rooms and temporary exhibitions (Casa de los Caballos building). Until then, only the archaeological rooms and the cistern are open.

claim: The Helga de Alvear museum is free to enter; hours are Tue-Sat 10:00-14:00 plus afternoons (17:00-20:00 Oct-May, 18:00-21:00 Jun-Sep) and Sun 10:00-14:30, closed Mondays; guided tours cost 5€ and are free Sunday mornings.
quote: admission to the Museum and exhibitions is free... October to May: Tuesday-Saturday: 10:00-14:00 and 17:00-20:00... June to September... 18:00-21:00... Sunday: 10:00-14:30. Closed Mondays

claim: The Helga de Alvear Collection is one of Europe's most important contemporary art collections, with over 3,000 works by 500+ artists including Picasso, Kandinsky, Louise Bourgeois, Ai Weiwei, Nan Goldin and Anish Kapoor.
quote: one of the most important collections of international contemporary art in Europe... more than 3,000 works by more than 500 artists... Louise Bourgeois, Kandinsky... Picasso, Tàpies, and Ai Weiwei... Nan Goldin, Jenny Holzer, Anish Kappor

claim: The Helga de Alvear museum opened spring 2021 in a Tuñón Arquitectos building with over 3,000 m² of exhibition space showing about 200 works from the collection.
quote: designed by award-winning Tuñón Arquitectos Studio, opened in spring 2021... more than 3,000 square metres of exhibition space, presenting a selection of around 200 works... by more than 100 international artists

claim: The Casa-Museo Árabe Yusuf Al-Burch is a restored 12th-century Arab house preserving an aljibe, hammam (Arab baths), interior courtyard and rooms with coins, weapons and crafts; open daily 10:30-14:00 plus afternoons (16:00-19:30 winter, 17:00-20:30 summer).
quote: an Arab house of origin constructed in the 12th century and restored... original spaces like the cistern (aljibe), the hammam (Arab baths)... Winter (October-April)... 4:00pm-7:30pm; Summer (May-September)... 5:00pm-8:30pm

claim: The Concatedral de Santa María offers a Cathedral Museum plus bell-tower panoramic views and the 1551 cedar-wood Renaissance altarpiece by Roque Balduque; general admission is 4€ (reduced 3-3.50€).
quote: visit the Cathedral Museum and enjoy a panoramic view of the Monumental City from the bell tower... retablo (altarpiece) of the Altar Mayor, a Renaissance work by Roque Balduque from 1551 made of cedar wood... General admission costs €4.00

claim: Casa Pedrilla houses a Museum of History and Culture tracing Extremadura from prehistory to today and the adjoining Guayasamín House-Museum holds pre-Columbian, colonial and original works of painter Oswaldo Guayasamín; open Tue-Sat 11:00-14:00 and 17:00-20:00, closed Mondays.
quote: the Guayasamín House-Museum houses a collection of pre-Columbian and colonial art compiled by the Ecuadorian painter and sculptor Oswaldo Guayasamín, including some of his own works... Tuesday to Saturday morning from 11:00 to 14:00, and in the afternoon from 17:00 to 20:00

claim: The Torre de Bujaco on Plaza Mayor houses the interpretation centre 'Tres momentos en la historia de Cáceres' covering Roman to medieval history; admission 2.50€ with access to the Arco de la Estrella and wall sections.
quote: an interpretation centre called "Tres momentos en la historia de Cáceres"... from its Roman foundation to the Middle Ages... The ticket price is €2.50... you can also go to the Arco de la Estrella, part of the wall
